Rashi on Yevamot 3b:10:1.hebrew: זדונה כרת - בפרשת עריות (ויקרא י״ח:כ״ט) כתיב בתר כולהו: ״ונכרתו הנפשות העושות״. וכל שזדונו כרת, שגגתו חטאת, כדיליף בפירקין (דף ט.):
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:10:1.english: Its intentional [violation incurs] karet - In the section of forbidden relations (Leviticus 18:29), it is written after all of them: "And the souls that commit [them] shall be cut off." And [for] any [transgression] whose intentional [violation incurs] karet, its unwitting [violation incurs] a sin-offering, as [the Gemara] derives in our chapter (page 9a).

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:11:1.hebrew: ט"ו נשים - תו ליכא עריות בכרת, חוץ משש עריות של משנתינו, שאין בהם צד ייבום לעולם:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:11:1.english: Fifteen women - There are no other forbidden relatives [punishable] by karet, except for the six forbidden relatives of our mishna, in which there is never an aspect of levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:12:1.hebrew: יכול שאני מרבה כו' - שנשואות לאחרים, שיהו צרותיהן אסורות לינשא לזה:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:12:1.english: I might [think] that I should include, etc. - [Where] they are married to other [men], that their rival wives should be forbidden to marry this [man].

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:14:1.hebrew: שאין צרה אלא מאח - הואיל ופטרה הכתוב מזיקתו, הרי היא עליו באיסור אשת אח שיש לה בנים, שהיא בכרת, דכתיב: ״ערות אשת אחיך״. אבל בעלמא, לא רמי' איסור אשת אח עלה, ושריא ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:14:1.english: For a rival wife is only from a brother - Since Scripture exempted her from his [levirate] bond, behold, she stands [forbidden] to him under the prohibition of a brother's wife who has children, which entails *karet*, as it is written: "The nakedness of your brother's wife" [Leviticus 18:16]. However, in general [where she was married to an unrelated man], the prohibition of a brother's wife is not cast upon her, and she is permitted to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:15:1.english: From where [is] the punishment [derived] - If he enters into levirate marriage with a forbidden relative or her rival wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:16:1.english: I would say [that] a wife’s sister enters into levirate marriage - [The reading is: the yavam] performs levirate marriage [with her].

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:16:2.english: What is the reason - For is he not subject to karet regarding her?

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:16:3.english: That a positive [commandment] comes - [That] of levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:16:4.english: And overrides a negative commandment - For we derive from Scripture that a positive [commandment] comes and overrides a negative commandment, as [the Gemara] proceeds to explain.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:1:1.hebrew: דרב ודרב אסי - דאמר רב: צרת סוטה אסורה, שאם זינתה אשתו ולו אשה אחרת ומת בלא בנים, שתיהן פטורות. ורב אסי אמר: צרת אילונית אסורה, שאם היה נשוי אילונית ואשה אחרת ומת בלא בנים, שתיהן פטורות. ותרוייהו בפירקין (דף יא.):
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:1:1.english: Of Rav and of Rav Asi - For Rav said: "The rival wife of a sota is forbidden" — that if his wife committed adultery and he had another wife, and he died without children, both of them are exempt. And Rav Asi said: "The rival wife of an aylonit is forbidden" — that if he was married to an aylonit and another wife, and he died without children, both of them are exempt. And both of them are in our chapter (11a).

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:2:1.hebrew: צרת ממאנת - הרי שהיה לאחיו יתומה קטנה ואשה אחרת, ומת, ומיאנה הקטנה ביבם זה — היא וצרתה אסורה לו. ומתני' אשמעי' דאף ע"ג דאסירא עליה, לא מיפטרה מחליצה, דהך איסורא מדרבנן היא, כדאיתא בפירקין — גזירה משום צרת בתו ממאנת:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:2:1.english: The rival wife of a woman who performs refusal - In a case where his brother had a minor orphan girl and another wife, and he died, and the minor performed refusal against this yavam — she and her rival wife are forbidden to him. And the Mishnah teaches us that even though she [the rival wife] is forbidden to him, she is not exempt from ḥalitza, for this prohibition is Rabbinic, as is stated in our chapter — a decree on account of the rival wife of his daughter who performs refusal.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:2:2.hebrew: מחזיר גרושתו - אחיו שגירש אחת משתי נשיו, ונשאת לאחר, ועבר והחזירה לאחר מיתת בעלה, ומת בלא בנים — שתיהן אסורות להתייבם. ואשמועינן מיעוטא דמתני' דחליצה בעיא:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:2:2.english: One who remarries his divorcée - His brother who divorced one of his two wives, and she married another [man], and he transgressed and remarried her after the death of her [second] husband, and died without children — both of them are forbidden to enter levirate marriage. And the exclusion of the mishna teaches us that she requires ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:4:1.hebrew: ליתנינהו - לסוטה ואילונית בהדי הנך דמתני', הואיל ופוטרות צרותיהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:4:1.english: Let [the Mishnah] teach them - [Namely,] a sotah and an aylonit, together with those of the Mishnah, since they exempt their co-wives.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:5:1.hebrew: לפי שאינן בצרת צרה - דכל הנך דמתני', איכא למיתני: הלכה צרתה ונשאת לאחיו השני כו' — שהרי אינה ערוה אלא לזה, אבל לאחיו השני ראויות הן. ואם ייבם, אפי' את הצרה, ולו אשה אחרת, ומת, ונפלו לפני זה — פטורה אף הנכרית, מפני שהיא צרת צרתה של בתו. אבל בסוטה ואילונית, ליכא למיתני: הלכה צרתה ונשאת לאחיו השני — דהא על כל האחין היא אסורה, ושהאיסור בא לה מכח קדושי בעלה הראשון, וכולן שוין בהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:5:1.english: Because they do not [involve the case of] a rival of a rival - For regarding all those [women] in the Mishnah, it is possible to teach: “If her rival went and married his second brother, etc.,” for she is a forbidden relation only to this [brother], but to his second brother they are permitted. And if [the second brother] performed levirate marriage even with [just] the rival, and he had another wife, and he died, and [both wives] fell before this [first brother], even the unrelated woman is exempt, because she is the rival of the rival of his daughter. But in the case of a *sotah* and an *aylonit*, it is not possible to teach: “If her rival went and married his second brother,” for she is forbidden to all the brothers, as the prohibition came upon her by virtue of the betrothal of her first husband, and all [the brothers] are equal regarding them.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:6:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That a forbidden relative, and her rival wife, and the rival wife of her rival wife, are forever exempt.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:6:2.hebrew: עליה מה תלמוד לומר - לכתוב ״לגלות ערותה בחייה״, ותשמע נמי שבחיי אשתו נאסרת עליו אחותה, ולאחר מיתה מותרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:6:2.english: "With her" — what does the verse teach? - Let [the verse] write "to uncover her nakedness in her lifetime," and it would also be understood that during his wife's lifetime her sister is forbidden to him, and after [her] death she is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:7:1.hebrew: שומע אני - אפי' נפלה לפניו לייבום אחת מן העריות, תתייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:7:1.english: I might understand - Even if one of the forbidden relations fell before him for levirate marriage, she would enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 3b:9:1.hebrew: לצרור - צרות הרבה משמע, מדלא כתיב לצור:
Rashi on Yevamot 3b:9:1.english: To be a rival - It implies multiple rival wives, since it is not written latzor.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:11:1.hebrew: מה אחות אשה מיוחדת כו' - וא"ת: מה לאחות אשה שכן בידו לרבות, כדפריך בפ' הבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות דף נד. ושם)? וי"ל: דאהיקש דר' יונה דסוף שמעתין (דף ח.) סמיך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:11:1.english: "Just as a wife's sister is specific, etc." - And if you say: What [comparison can be made] to a wife's sister, for it is in his power to multiply [the prohibitions], as [the Gemara] asks in the chapter [entitled] Haba Al Yevamto (below, Yevamot 54a, and there)? And one can say that [the Baraita] relies on the hekesh [scriptural analogy] of Rabbi Yonah at the end of our sugya (8a).

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:12:1.hebrew: יכול שאני מרבה אף שש עריות חמורות מאלו - המ"ל: יכול שאני מרבה אף שלא במקום מצוה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:12:1.english: "One might think that I should include even six forbidden relations more severe than these" - [The baraita] could have said: "One might think that I should include [rival wives] even not in the context of a mitzvah."

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:16:1.hebrew: טעמא דכתב רחמנא עליה הא לאו הכי הוה אמינא אחות אשה מייבמת - ותימה לר"י, דמנא ליה? הא נימא דאי לאו "עליה" נמי אחות אשה לא מתייבמת, דאין עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, ואיצטריך "עליה" למיסר לאשמעינן דבעלמא דחי? דכה"ג אמר לקמן: טעמא דכתב רחמנא "את שבתותי תשמורו", הא לאו הכי דחי! וכ"ת דא"שומע אני" דברייתא קפריך, דמשמע לישנא דאי לאו "עליה" ה"א דדחי — א"כ, מאי משני רבא בסוף מסקנא: "ערוה גופיה לא צריכא קרא, דאין עשה דוחה ל"ת שיש בו כרת"? אלא ע"כ, "שומע אני" לאו דוקא, והכי קאמר: אם ת"ל דדחי, הא כתיב "עליה", ומיהו עיקרא לאו להכי אתא. ואר"י, דאי בעלמא אין עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, לא ה"ל לתנא למדרש "עליה" לאיסורא, ולא יצטרך לגופיה אלא לאשמעינן דבעלמא דחי; אלא ה"ל למידרש להיתירא: נאמר כאן "עליה" ונאמר להלן "עליה", מה להלן באחות אשה אף כאן באחות אשה, ואמר רחמנא: "יבמה יבא עליה", דמסתבר טפי למדרש הכי ולאוקמי קרא לגופיה. אלא ודאי, סבר האי תנא עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, ולא צריך קרא להיתירא, ולהכי דריש ליה לגופיה לאיסורא. ורב אשי דפריך לקמן (יבמות דף ח:): "ממאי דהאי 'עליה' לאיסורא, דילמא להיתירא?" — ארבא דמסיק דאין עשה דוחה ל"ת שיש בו כרת פריך, כמו שפי' ר"י ברבי מאיר; אבל כל כמה דס"ד דדחי, לא מצי למיפרך הכי. ורבא לא הוה צ"ל: "אלא להיתירא לא מצית אמרת, דא"כ 'לגלות ערותה' דחדא היכי משכחת לה", כדמשני לקמן אקושיא דרב אשי, דעיקר דקדוק הש"ס הוא מכח דלא דריש להיתירא; אלא לפי דעתו של מקשה היה פשוט דעשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, השיב לו רבא האמת, דאינו כן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:16:1.english: "The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'with her'; had it not been so, I would say a wife's sister enters into levirate marriage" - And it is astounding to the Ri: From where does [the Gemara] know this? Let us rather say that even without "with her," a wife's sister would also not enter into levirate marriage, because a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment that entails karet; and "with her" was necessary to prohibit [her in levirate marriage] in order to teach us that elsewhere [a positive commandment] does override [a prohibition] of this type! For similarly [the Gemara] states below [6a]: "The reason is that the Merciful One wrote: 'And you shall keep My Sabbaths' [Leviticus 19:3]; had it not been so, it would override!" And if you should say that [the Gemara] is raising a difficulty based on the "I would derive" [shome'a ani] of the baraita [3b], which implies by its wording that were it not for "with her," I would say that it overrides — if so, what is [the meaning of] what Rava answers in the final conclusion [8a]: "A forbidden relative herself does not need a verse, for a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment that entails karet"? Rather, perforce, "I would derive" is not meant literally, and this is what it means: If you could say that it overrides, behold, "with her" is written; however, primarily it did not come for this [but rather to prohibit her rival wife]. And the Ri says: That if elsewhere [in general] a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment that entails karet, the tanna should not have expounded "with her" to prohibit [her], such that [the verse] would not be needed for its own subject except to teach us that elsewhere [a positive commandment] overrides. Rather, he should have expounded it to permit: It is stated here [in Deuteronomy 25:5 regarding levirate marriage]: "upon her" [aleha], and it is stated there [in Leviticus 18:18 regarding a wife's sister]: "upon her" [aleha]. Just as there [in Leviticus 18:18] it speaks of a wife's sister, so too here [in Deuteronomy 25:5] it speaks of a wife's sister, and the Merciful One states: "her brother-in-law shall go in unto her" [Deuteronomy 25:5]! For it is more reasonable to expound it in this way, and establish the verse for its own subject. Rather, certainly, this tanna maintains that a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment that entails karet, and [therefore] a verse was not needed to permit [her]; and for this reason, he expounded it for its own subject to prohibit [her]. And Rav Ashi, who asks below (Yevamot 8b): "From where [is it derived] that this 'with her' is to prohibit? Perhaps it is to permit?" — he asks according to Rava, who concludes that a positive commandment does not override a negative commandment that entails karet, as explained by Rabbeinu Yitzḥak bar Meir; however, as long as it entered our mind that it overrides, he could not ask this. And Rava did not need to say [to the questioner]: "Rather, you cannot say [that it comes] to permit, for if so, under what circumstances would you find [that] 'to uncover her nakedness' [Leviticus 18:18] refers to one [sister alone]?" — as [the Gemara] answers below [8b] to the difficulty of Rav Ashi, since the primary deduction of the Talmud [on 3b] is by virtue of [the fact that the tanna] does not expound it to permit; rather, in the view of the questioner, it was obvious that a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment that entails karet, [and so] Rava answered him the true reality, that it is not so.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:17:1.hebrew: לא תעשה שיש בו כרת מי דחי - וא"ת: ואמאי לא ילפינן דלידחי מעשה דייבום, דדחי לא תעשה דכרת דאשת אח? וכ"ת: דהיינו הא דקאמר לקמן (יבמות דף ז.): "אלא איצטריך, סד"א תיתי אחות אשה במה מצינו מאשת אח" — דא"כ, היכי דחי עלה: "מי דמי? התם חדא איסורא, הכא תרי איסורי"? הא לא מפלגינן בשום מקום וילפינן מכלאים בציצית; אפי' תרי איסורי היכי בעי למילף?! ועוד, דלקמן כי בעי למילף מפסח, תמיד ומילה, לא פרכינן הכי. ועוד, דשביק הש"ס אשת אח דקאי בה, ולא מסיק לה אלא לבסוף. ועוד, דחדא איסורא מיהא נילף מאשת אח! אלא על כרחך, לקמן לאו בכל דוכתי בעי למילף מאשת אח קאתי, אלא דוקא אחות אשה, כדמסיק טעמא: "הואיל ואישתרי אישתרי". ולהכי קאמר: "תיתי אחות אשה מאשת אח", ולא קאמר "תיתי מאשת אח", כדאמר בכל הני דלקמן: "תיתי ממילה", "תיתי מכיבוד אב", ואינו מזכיר אחות אשה — משום דלמילף בכל דוכתין קאתי. ואומר ר"י, דמאשת אח לא מצי למילף בעלמא דלידחי עשה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת, דשאני אשת אח דמצותו בכך, ואי אפשר בענין אחר לקיים מצות יבום, דאל"כ בטלה מצות יבום. אבל מכלאים בציצית ילפי' שפיר בעלמא, דאי לא מקיימת מצות תכלת בפשתי' מקיימת בצמר, ואפ"ה דחי. וכן "וגלח את כל שערו" דמצורע מיקיים בשער דהיתר, דכל שערו קרינא ביה, כמו "כל מלאכה לא תעשו" דשבת דלא קאי אלא אמלאכות דלא דחו שבת; א"נ, כל שערו ממש, ובנמרטו פאת ראשו וזקנו. וכן כל הני דמייתו מיקיימי בדוכתא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:17:1.english: Does [a positive mitzva] override a negative precept that entails karet? - And if you say: And why do we not derive that it should override from the positive mitzva of levirate marriage (yibbum), which overrides the negative precept punishable by karet of a brother's wife (eshet aḥ)? And if you say that this is indeed that which [the Gemara] says later (Yevamot 7b): "Rather, it is necessary, [for] it could enter your mind to say: Let a wife's sister be derived by a mah matzinu [analogy] from a brother's wife" — for if so, how does [the Gemara] reject it [by asking]: "Is it comparable? There [in the case of a brother's wife] it is one prohibition, [whereas] here [in the case of a wife's sister] there are two prohibitions"? Behold, we do not distinguish anywhere [and say that] we derive from [the case of] diverse kinds in ritual fringes [that an aseh overrides] even two prohibitions; [so] how could [the Gemara] seek to derive [that yibbum overrides two prohibitions]?! And furthermore, later [on 5b–6a], when [the Gemara] seeks to derive [that a positive mitzva overrides a prohibition punishable by karet] from the Paschal offering, the daily offering, and circumcision, we do not raise this objection. And furthermore, the Gemara leaves aside [the case of] a brother's wife, which it is [presently] dealing with, and does not raise it until the very end [on 7b]! And furthermore, at least [for] a single prohibition [punishable by karet], let us derive [that a positive mitzva overrides it] from a brother's wife! Rather, perforce, later [on 7b, the Gemara] does not come to derive [a general rule] for all places from a brother's wife, but specifically [to permit] a wife's sister, as it concludes the reason: "Since it was permitted [in part], it was permitted [entirely]" (ho'il ve'ishtarei ishtarei). And that is why it says: "Let a wife's sister be derived from a brother's wife," and does not say [generally]: "Let it be derived from a brother's wife," as it says in all those cases later [on 5b–6a]: "Let it be derived from circumcision," "Let it be derived from honoring father [and mother]," where it does not mention a wife's sister — because [there] it comes to derive [a general rule] for all places. And the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] says that from a brother's wife one cannot derive generally that a positive mitzva should override a negative precept that entails karet, for a brother's wife is different, since its mitzva is [inherently defined] in this manner, and it is impossible to fulfill the mitzva of levirate marriage in any other way, for if not so, the mitzva of levirate marriage would be nullified. However, from [the case of] diverse kinds in ritual fringes we can well derive [a principle] generally, for if you do not fulfill the mitzva of sky-blue wool (tekhelet) on linen [garments], you could fulfill it on wool [garments], and even so it overrides. And similarly, "And he shall shave all his hair" (Leviticus 14:9) regarding a leper (metzora) could be fulfilled on permissible hair, for we would still read in it "all his hair," just as "You shall not do any work" (Exodus 20:10) regarding Shabbat applies only to labors that do not override Shabbat; or alternatively, [it could be fulfilled on] literally all his hair, in [a case where] the corners of his head and beard were plucked out. And similarly, all those [mitzvot] that they bring [later in the Gemara as potential sources] can be fulfilled in another context.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:1:1.hebrew: למעוטי דרב ודרב אסי - וא"ת: לימעט תרוייהו ממנינא דרישא! דכיון דתנן ט"ו נשים, ליכא למימר שייר, וממעטי כולהו מדלא קתני להו — כדאמר בפ"ק דקדושין (דף טז:): "וכ"ת תנא ושייר — והא ארבעה קתני!" וי"ל: דהכא לא מצי למיתנינהו, כדמסיק: "לפי שאינן בצרת צרה", וליכא למעוטי מדלא קתני להו, אלא מייתורא דמתני'. וטעמא דרב אסי ודפליג עליה — אפרש לקמן בע"ה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:1:1.english: "To exclude [the rulings] of Rav and of Rav Asi" - And if you say: Let both of them be excluded from the count in the first clause [reisha], for since the Mishnah teaches "Fifteen women," one cannot say that [the Tanna] omitted [cases], and all [other cases] would be excluded [simply] from the fact that he did not teach them — as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Kiddushin (16b): "And if you say [the Tanna] taught [some] and omitted [others] — but doesn't he teach four?!" And one can say [in reply]: Here, [the Tanna] could not have taught them, as [the Gemara] concludes [later]: "Because they do not [apply to the case of] a rival wife of a rival wife," and [therefore] they cannot be excluded [simply] from the fact that he did not teach them, but rather from the superfluity of the Mishnah. And the reasoning of Rav Asi and of the one who disagrees with him I will explain below, with God's help.

Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:5:1.hebrew: לפי שאינן בצרת צרה - וא"ת: דמשכחת לה צרת צרה לענין בועל — שנשאת לאחיו ולו אשה אחרת, ומת בלא בנים, דפוטרת צרתה מן הבועל, דלענין בועל נמי טומאה בה כמו לענין בעל; ואם הלכה הצרה ונשאת לאחיו השני ולו אשה אחרת, ומת — כשם שהיא פטורה, כך צרתה פטורה! וי"ל: דכיון דלגבי בעל לא משכחת צרת צרה, אין לנו להחמיר בטומאה דגבי בועל יותר מטומאה דגבי הבעל. ועוד אר"י: דדוקא בטומאה דכתיב גבי בעל הוי כעריות, דכתיב בלשון לאו: "לא יוכל בעלה וגו'" (דברים כ״ד:ד׳); אבל בבועל לא כתיב לאו, אלא "ונסתרה והיא נטמאה" (במדב' ה). והא דפריך לקמן (יבמות ד' יא:): "נבעלה, טומאה כתיבה בה, ונסתרה והיא נטמאה", דמשמע דמהאי לחודיה דריש "טומאה כתיב בה כעריות" — מצית למימר: דלמאי דמשני "למיקם עלה בלאו", לא סגי בההוא ד"ונסתרה והיא נטמאה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 3b:5:1.english: "Because they do not [involve the case of] a rival wife of a rival wife" - And if you say: But one can find [a case of] a rival wife of a rival wife with regard to an adulterer [bo'el] — [namely,] where she married his brother, and [the brother] had another wife, and he died without children, so that she exempts her rival wife from the adulterer, as regarding the adulterer as well, "defilement" is written concerning her just as regarding the husband; and if that rival wife went and married his second brother, and he had another wife, and he died — just as she [the first rival wife] is exempt, so her rival wife [the second rival wife] should be exempt! And one can say: Since with regard to the husband one does not find [a case of] a rival wife of a rival wife, we should not be more stringent regarding the defilement in the case of the adulterer than regarding the defilement in the case of the husband. And furthermore, the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] said: Specifically regarding the defilement written concerning the husband is it considered like forbidden relations [arayot], because it is written in the formulation of a negative commandment: "Her former husband... may not [take her again]" etc. (Deuteronomy 24:4); but regarding the adulterer, a negative commandment is not written, but rather, "and she was secluded and defiled" (Numbers 5:13). And as for that which [the Gemara] challenges below (Yevamot 11b): "[If] she engaged in relations, defilement is written concerning her: 'and she was secluded and defiled,'" which implies that from this [verse] alone it derives that "defilement is written concerning her like forbidden relations" — you can say: According to what [the Gemara] answers, "[it is needed] to establish a negative commandment upon her," that [verse] of "and she was secluded and defiled" does not suffice [on its own].
